prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single objectively “best” roofing company for every Miami home — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget, insurance situation and whether you need a tile, shingle, metal or flat/hot-mopped system. I can find top-rated local contractors for you if you give me your ZIP code. Meanwhile, here’s how to find the best hurricane-rated roofer in Miami and what to verify.

What to look for (must-haves)
- Florida roofing license (check on the Florida DBPR site). Prefer a Certified Roofing Contractor.  
- Miami‑Dade/HVHZ experience: Miami is in the High‑Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ). Make sure the contractor and the products/install methods meet Miami‑Dade County and Florida Building Code HVHZ requirements.  
- Manufacturer certification (e.g., GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT). Certified installers can back manufacturer warranties.  
- Use of Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved materials (Product Control Notice of Acceptance numbers for shingles/tiles/fasteners).  
- Adequate insurance: general liability (commonly $1M+) and workers’ compensation. Verify current certificates.  
- Written, itemized proposal that includes scope, materials (with NOA numbers if applicable), permitting, disposal, timelines, payment schedule, and warranty details (manufacturer + workmanship).  
- Local references and recent HVHZ project photos; ask for addresses of recent jobs so you can inspect.  
- Will they obtain permits and handle inspections? (They should.)  
- Good online ratings and long local track record; check BBB, Google, Yelp, and county records for complaints.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed, and can I see your DBPR license number?  
- Do you have experience with Miami‑Dade/HVHZ installations? Examples?  
- Which products do you recommend for high-wind resistance and why? (Ask about wind ratings and NOA approvals.)  
- Are you factory‑certified for that product? What warranties come with the installation?  
- Do you handle permits and inspections? Will you provide lien waivers?  
- What is your start/finish timeline and clean‑up policy?  
- How do you handle storm/emergency tarping and insurance claims?

Red flags
- Demands for large upfront cash payment only.  
- No written contract or vague scope.  
- No DBPR license, no insurance proof, or unwillingness to provide references.  
- Very low bid that’s much lower than other estimates — could indicate use of substandard materials or unlicensed labor.

Types of hurricane‑resistant roofing to consider
- Metal panels / standing seam: excellent wind performance when properly installed.  
- Tile (concrete/terracotta): heavy; needs correct fastening and secondary water barrier.  
- High‑wind rated architectural shingles: look for Miami‑Dade NOA approvals and high wind ratings.  
- Modified bitumen / single‑ply membranes for low‑slope roofs (must be HVHZ‑rated systems).

How I can help right now
- If you give your ZIP code or neighborhood and tell me roof type (tile, shingle, metal, flat), I’ll research and provide a short list (3–5) of highly rated Miami-area companies that match your needs, plus quick checks of license, certifications, and recent reviews.

Would you like me to find local options for your ZIP code?
